en: Section B interview.
zh: B节：访谈。

en: In this section you will hear one interview.
zh: 在这一节中，你将听到一段访谈。

en: The interview will be divided into two parts.
zh: 这段访谈分为两部分。

en: At the end of each part, five questions will be asked about what was said.
zh: 每部分结束后，将就刚才所说的内容提出五个问题。

en: Both the interview and the questions will be spoken once only.
zh: 访谈和问题都只读一遍。

en: After each question, there will be a ten-second pause.
zh: 每个问题之后会有十秒钟的停顿。

en: During the pause you should read the four choices of A, B, C and D and mark the best answer to each question on answer sheet 2.
zh: 请利用停顿时间阅读A、B、C、D四个选项，并在答题卡二上标出每题的最佳答案。

en: You have 30 seconds to preview the choices.
zh: 你有三十秒钟预览选项。

en: Now listen to part one of the Interview.
zh: 现在请听访谈的第一部分。

en: Questions one to five are based on part one of the interview.
zh: 第1至5题根据访谈的第一部分提问。

en: Good evening, listeners.
zh: 各位听众，晚上好。

en: This is BBC.
zh: 这里是英国广播公司。

en: Today, we are very delighted to have invited James Dobbins, U.S. special representative for Afghanistan, to tell us the electoral process in Afghanistan currently.
zh: 今天，我们非常高兴邀请到美国阿富汗问题特别代表詹姆斯·多宾斯，请他谈谈阿富汗目前的选举进程。

en: Well, James, how are you reading what’s happening in Afghanistan at the moment?
zh: 詹姆斯，你如何解读阿富汗眼下的局势呢？

en: We’re concerned about the trend in events.
zh: 我们很关心事态的发展趋势。

en: We have been concerned for some time that the electoral process hasn’t been moving forward smoothly.
zh: 一段时间以来，我们一直担心，选举进程没有顺利推进。

en: We believe there needs to be a powerful and transparent audit of potentially dishonest ballots
zh: 我们认为，有必要对涉嫌舞弊的选票进行有力且透明的审查；

en: and we’re sorry that hasn’t moved forward quickly and substantially enough.
zh: 遗憾的是，这件事推进得还不够快、也不够充分。

en: We regret the preliminary announcement of results that was made yesterday.
zh: 我们对昨天公布初步结果一事感到遗憾。

en: We think that was premature given that there are still a number of ballots that need to be examined and there’s not yet a clear agreement on how best to do so.
zh: 我们认为这为时过早，因为仍有大量选票需要检查，而且大家尚未就最佳处理办法达成明确共识。

en: We do believe that—
zh: 我们确实认为……

en: Forgive me for interrupting, James.
zh: 詹姆斯，请原谅我打断一下。

en: Can I ask you why you think that announcement was made yesterday?
zh: 能否问一下，你认为昨天为什么会发布那项公告？

en: I think it was made because the electoral institution had previously set that date
zh: 我认为，这是因为选举机构事先定好了那个日期；

en: and they held to it despite advice to the contrary from the UN, from the United States, and from other voices within Afghanistan,
zh: 尽管联合国、美国以及阿富汗国内其他方面提出了相反建议，它们仍坚持原定日期，

en: and we think that was unfortunate.
zh: 我们认为这很不妥。

en: Is there another reason that could be slightly more favorable,
zh: 能否从稍微有利的角度来解释呢？

en: that is, they wanted to prepare the ground because if they just came out with one final result at the end of all this,
zh: 也许它们是想先做铺垫，因为如果一直等到最后才公布一个最终结果，

en: then it can be pretty likely that the loser, whoever it was going to be, was going to complain because they think it is unfair?
zh: 那么无论谁落败，都很可能会抱怨结果不公平。

en: I think it’s our view that they didn’t have a basis for preparing the ground because there’s such a large number of votes that still need to be examined and
zh: 我们的看法是，它们并不具备作这种铺垫的依据，因为仍有那么多选票等待检查；

en: that therefore any preliminary result might be more misleading than preparing the ground.
zh: 因此，任何初步结果都可能不是在作铺垫，而是在误导公众。

en: In terms now of where this goes, we’ve already heard some very strong, very emotional language
zh: 那么接下来会如何发展呢？我们已经听到一些非常强烈、情绪激动的言论，

en: from the camp of the man who appears to be on the losing side of all this, Dr. Abdullah Abdullah.
zh: 这些言论来自看起来可能落败的阿卜杜拉·阿卜杜拉博士所在的阵营。

en: What have you been saying to him in order to try and calm those feelings?
zh: 为了平复这些情绪，你们一直在对他说些什么呢？

en: Well, we have heard talk about establishing a parallel presidency.
zh: 我们听到有人在讨论另设一个平行的总统政权。

en: We made clear that the United States and its partners are not in a position to support a divided Afghanistan.
zh: 我们已经明确表示，美国及其伙伴无法支持一个分裂的阿富汗。

en: That any effort to establish a parallel presidency
zh: 任何建立平行总统政权的尝试，

en: would make it impossible for the United States and its partners to continue their financial, economic and military support,
zh: 都会使美国及其伙伴无法继续提供财政、经济和军事支持，

en: and that the consequences for the country would be potentially quite terrible.
zh: 而这可能给阿富汗带来非常严重的后果。

en: Clearly, this is not something the Afghan population wants.
zh: 显然，阿富汗民众不希望看到这种情况。

en: It’s not something they were voting for.
zh: 他们投票也不是为了得到这样的结果。

en: And it’s not something that they expect to happen, but it could be the consequences of an ill-considered action.
zh: 他们并不期待这种情况发生，但考虑不周的行动可能会造成这样的后果。

en: This is the end of part one of the interview.
zh: 访谈的第一部分到此结束。

en: Questions one to five are based on what you have just heard.
zh: 第1至5题根据你刚才听到的内容提问。

en: Question 1. Which aspect of the election event is the interviewee most concerned about?
zh: 第1题：受访者最关心选举事件的哪个方面？

en: Question 2. Why was the announcement made yesterday, according to the interviewee?
zh: 第2题：根据受访者的说法，昨天为什么会发布公告？

en: Question 3. According to the BBC interviewer, why did the electoral institutions want to prepare the ground?
zh: 第3题：根据BBC采访者的说法，选举机构为什么想提前作铺垫？

en: Question 4. What did the interviewee think of the BBC’s reason of preparing the ground?
zh: 第4题：受访者如何看待BBC提出的“提前作铺垫”这一理由？

en: Question 5. What is the interviewee’s attitude towards establishing a parallel presidency?
zh: 第5题：受访者对另设平行总统政权持什么态度？
